content.comment_body: Hello. A year ago, we bought a [product_name] and several accessories: [product_name] AM2 PT100 Module, [product_name] TD, two PT1000 probes, and [product_name] Soft Comfort (Italian version). The connection diagram was sourced from [url], and the FDB setup references the user guide: AI5, B001 (Analog Amp, PT100/PT1000, Gain = 2.5+, Offset = 500, Point = 1), B002 (Signal Text, B001, amplified). Unfortunately, the [product_name] always displays the same readings on both probes regardless of temperature. I changed the probes, but this made no difference. Could this fault be with the [product_name] or the AM2 PT100 module? How should I proceed with testing?

Hello, What is the part number for your [product_name]? If your setup has 2 onboard analog inputs, the first one on the AM module will be AI3; if there are 4 onboard analog inputs, inputs 3 or 5 can be configured in the software. To check the module's status, observe the display and verify if analog input values appear.
Just to clarify: the AM2 PT100 module works only with PT100 sensors, while the AM2 RTD module supports PT100 or PT1000 sensors. Please consult the handbook for details.
You're right, I missed that the sensor is PT1000. Thanks for pointing that out.

I read the AM2 PT100 datasheet and followed the instructions for connecting a Pt100/Pt1000 sensor, assuming it supported Pt1000. Can I use two AM2 modules together (AM2PT100 + AM2RTD)? If I purchase an AM2 RTD module for the two Pt1000 probes, can I also buy two PT100 sensors to use with my AM2 PT100? I’d like to monitor four temperatures simultaneously. How many AM2 modules can be connected at once to my [product_name]?

Hello, According to the manual: Maximum expansion and communication module configuration for [product_name] supports up to 24 digital inputs, 8 analog inputs, 16 digital outputs, and 2 analog outputs. So you can use both modules with your device.
I can't find the AM2 RTD module. My supplier does not have it available. Checking [url] for modular expansion modules, but I don’t see an RTD module listed. Can someone share the part number?
Hello, It should be this one: [url]

Correct! The [company_name] website has outdated and incomplete information, but the iPhone App is completely up to date. Through the App, I discovered the AM2 PT100 is obsolete and was replaced by the AM2 RTD in 2010. The App provides the correct order codes for the modules. Website is not helpful – App wins.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced inaccurate temperature readings due to using a PT100-only module with PT1000 sensors, highlighting confusion around module compatibility. The documentation and product availability online was insufficient, but the mobile app provided accurate product information and helped users identify the correct modules and order codes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect accurate sensor readings, clear documentation explaining module-probe compatibility, and reliable, easy-to-access product information and order numbers.
